scope: Portable issuer-signed machine identity credentials, key epochs, rotation/recovery history, revocation records and supplied-evidence currentness. This model does not promote legal identity, global currentness, reputation or runtime authority.
core_invariant: A machine identity credential proves only the reviewed issuer/key/principal continuity encoded by the credential and supplied lifecycle evidence. It does not grant authority, prove legal personhood, truth, reputation or global currentness.

risks: sign with a different operational private key
present predecessor as current after rotation
controls: A6 retained latest-head currentness for new-effect decisions

risks: reuse operational key across rotation epochs
bind credential to broader principal definition
change sponsor/runtime/authority digest while preserving identity label
controls: A2 reproduces the same canonical principal commitment
A6 retained checkpoint chain detects omitted retained revocation evidence

known_nonclaims: A1 does not grant execution or delegation authority.
A1 does not prove legal identity or personhood.
A1 does not prove reputation, competence or truth.
A1 currentness is limited to the exact supplied issuer evidence.
A1 alone does not detect retained-head rollback across independent restart; A6a supplies a laboratory primitive for that purpose.
A1 does not modify the production capability registry.
next_gates: independent security review of identity lifecycle and canonicalization
authoritative capability-registry entry only after ATP promotion review
bind independently retained currentness evidence before consequential effects
